chunks: Ahmad ibn Ishaq wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

that Durrah, daughter of Muqatil, had died and left an estate — shares of land in various places — and she had bequeathed to her master from her shares an amount exceeding one-third. We are her executors and wished to report to our master: if he commanded that the bequest be executed as it stands, we would execute it; and if he commanded otherwise, we would comply with his command in everything he commands, Allah Willing.

He said: So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'It is not obligatory for her from her estate except one-third; and if you are generous, and you are the inheritors, it would be permissible for you, Allah Willing.'

key_terms.أَشْقَاص: Shares or portions of jointly-owned property distributed across locations
key_terms.أَوْصِيَاء: Executors of a will; those entrusted to carry out a deceased person's bequest
key_terms.الثُّلُث: One-third; the maximum fraction of an estate that Islamic law permits to be disposed of by bequest
key_terms.الْوَرَثَة: Legal heirs; those entitled to inherit under Islamic succession law
key_terms.تَرِكَة: The estate left behind by a deceased person
key_terms.تَفَضَّل: To act generously or graciously beyond what is required
key_terms.ضَيْعَة: An agricultural estate or landed property

ai.seo_question: What does Islamic law say about bequeathing more than one-third of one's estate in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written legal inquiry sent by Ahmad ibn Ishaq to Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS) regarding a woman named Durrah bint Muqatil who died having bequeathed more than one-third of her estate to her master (sayyid). The Imam replied in his own handwriting confirming the foundational Islamic legal rule that only one-third of the estate may be validly bequeathed without the heirs' consent, while noting that if the heirs themselves are generous and willing, they may permit more. This ruling reflects the well-established principle in Islamic law (fiqh) that a testator's power of bequest is limited to one-third of the estate, protecting the rights of legal heirs.
